title: World Map
subtitle: Base game map · start {date}
loadFailed: The map could not be loaded: {reason}
hint: Click the map to see its province, state and strategic region. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, double-click to see the whole map.
whereRow: This state is in the project: the name is kept in its row in the States workbench and exported with the states' localisation.
whereRewrite: Exported to each language's replace localisation, over the game's name; the game preview shows it too.
namesUpdateSoon: The names on the map update in a few seconds
sketchTitle: A map from a sketch (try it)
sketchIntro: Download the blank canvas, paint land, mountains, forests… in the legend's colours with any drawing tool (no need to be neat), upload it, and see the game map it becomes.
sketchSummary: {width}×{height} · {land} land provinces · {sea} sea provinces · {lake} lakes · {seconds} s
noFindings: Every check passes (colours, connected provinces, junctions, water line, terrain indexes…)
notSaved: This is a trial: nothing is saved to the project. Adding new land to the base map, or making a whole world with it, comes in later steps.
sketchEmpty: Upload a sketch and press Generate
landTitle: Add new land on the sea
landIntro: Paint a sketch of the new land in the legend's colours, upload it, drag out where it goes on the map, preview the provinces and states it makes, then draw it into the project's map. Every base-game province keeps its number; new land only goes on the sea.
landFrameHint: Drag on the map with the left button to frame the new land (kept to the sketch's shape); drag inside the frame to move it, drag with the right button to pan, scroll to zoom.
landSummary: {land} land provinces · {water} water provinces cut off · {states} states · new numbers from {first}
landCovered: Takes part of these sea provinces (they keep their numbers): {list}
landIgnored: {pixels} pixels of the sketch fall on land or lakes already there and were left out
landNoFindings: Checks pass: nothing the map did not already have
landName: Name of the new land (states, strategic region)
landSaveNote: Writes the project's map files (province, height, terrain and river maps and their companions) and the new states; they ship with the export.
landNoneYet: None yet: the project uses the base game's map.
landRestore: Back to the base game's map
landRestoreTitle: Back to the base game's map?
landSketchUnreadable: The sketch could not be read: it must be a PNG or JPEG
landSavedBody: The new states are in the states workbench; make a country in the countries workbench and set its capital in its start history to play it.
landRestored: The base game's map is back
landOwnerHint: The game expects every state to have an owner: if you leave this empty, set the new states' owner later in the states workbench (your new country, say).
subtitleWithLand: Base game map + {count} pieces of new land · start {date}
editKindNote: Land can safely become sea or lake; a water province beside land can be raised and joined to a state. Use New land for an isolated island.
editPickHint: Click on the map: its state or strategic region is taken.
editNote: Written to the project's map files (definition.csv, strategic regions) and states; 「Back to the base game's map」 under New land takes it back too.
landRestoreBodyLand: Deletes the map files, the new states (with any later edits) and the names of {count} additions.
landUndoLand: Undo “{name}”: its map files, new states (with any later edits) and names go, and the map is as it was before it.
landUndoEdit: Undo the edit of province #{id}: back as it was before.
subtitleWithEdits: Base game map, {edits} province edits · start {date}
subtitleWithLandAndEdits: Base game map + {count} pieces of new land, {edits} province edits · start {date}
landAutoPreview: As soon as there is a sketch and a frame, the preview runs and the new land is drawn on the map.
landNeedSketch: First choose a sketch in step 1 (or the sample island).
landNeedFrame: Drag out where the new land goes on the map (step 2).
landNeedPreview: Wait for the preview before saving (step 3).
landBlocked: The preview found something that would break the map: move the frame or change the sketch.
landOwnerShort: The owner needs all three letters, or nothing.
worldIntro: Make a whole world from a sketch, from the base game’s provinces regrouped, or from a finished map you upload, and split its states between the countries you pick. The base game’s states, country starts, focus trees, events and more are unloaded (listed below); the base game map can be restored at any time.
worldStudioLink: Not into drawing programs? Paint it on the GameView map ↗
worldSourceGameNote: The base game’s 13,000-odd provinces are grouped into new states and strategic regions; the map pictures stay as they are.
worldCountriesHint: The states go to these countries from west to east (up to 8); change them later in the states workbench. A country has to exist in the countries workbench first.
worldPreviewing: Making the whole map, about 20 seconds…
worldPreviewHint: Pick the map and the countries, then preview how the states are split.
worldSummary: {land} land provinces · {sea} sea provinces · {states} states · {regions} strategic regions
worldOwnStart: {tag} already has a start: its capital moves into the new world (and back on restore).
worldUnloadIntro: The export unloads all of this base game content; the new world brings a bookmark, a default focus tree and a rewritten tutorial:
worldReplacedStates: The project’s {count} states are replaced by the new world’s; restoring the base game map puts them back as they were.
worldConfirm: I understand this base game content is unloaded
worldSaving: Writing it into the project, about a minute…
worldSaveNote: Writes the project’s map files, their companions and the new states; they ship with the export.
worldBlocked: The preview found something that would break the map: change the sketch and try again.
worldIsWorld: This project is already a new world: {states} states, countries {tags}.
worldNotBase: The map already has new land or province edits: restore the base game map first, then make a whole world.
worldSaved: The new world is in the project
worldSavedBody: {states} states; keep editing states and countries in their workbenches.
worldUndoWorld: Undo the new world: its map files and states go, and the project’s own states and country capitals come back.
worldSourceSketchNote: Paint a sketch in the legend’s colours; the program makes the provinces, heights and terrain.
worldSourceUploadNote: For map makers: your own province, height and terrain maps.
worldUploadHint: All three are 5632×2048 (the base game map’s size), PNG or BMP (not JPEG for the province map); the terrain map uses colours from the base game terrain.bmp palette. The river map and definition.csv are optional: without definition.csv every colour is a province and heights under 95 are water.
worldNeedUpload: Choose the province, height and terrain maps first
worldMadeDefinitions: No definition.csv: one was made, water from the heightmap and land terrain from the terrain map.
worldMadeRivers: No river map: one without rivers was made.
